messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The failure in the test org.apache.commons.lang.time.DurationFormatUtilsTest.testJiraLang281() is due to an incorrect result returned by DurationFormatUtils.formatPeriod when formatting the period between Dec 31, 2005 and Oct 6, 2006 with the format "MM".

The method DurationFormatUtils.formatPeriod(long startMillis, long endMillis, String format, boolean padWithZeros, TimeZone timezone) performs the following steps:

1. It computes the difference in milliseconds and if less than 28 days uses formatDuration instead.
2. It tokenizes the format string.
3. Creates Calendar instances for the start and end timestamps.
4. Calculates initial differences for each time field (millis, seconds, minutes, hours, days, months, years).
5. Adjusts these differences so none are negative by borrowing from higher fields.
6. Calls reduceAndCorrect to correct differences by adjusting the 'end' calendar and rechecking values for each field.
7. Adjusts fields based on which tokens are present in the format string, collapsing years into months or months into days if needed.

The bug pertains to how days are adjusted in the while (days < 0) loop in formatPeriod. The code currently blindly adds 31 days when days is negative, assuming months have 31 days (line 306). However, months have variable length (28-31 days), and adding 31 days regardless causes incorrect negative month differences when the start date is at the end of December (31st) and the end date is in October of the next year.

Because the test uses Dec 31 (month = 11, day = 31) as start and Oct 6 (month = 9) as end, this causes the negative day offset to be incorrectly adjusted, resulting in a month difference of -2 instead of 9.

The reduceAndCorrect calls that follow also interact with this miscalculation, but the root cause is the static addition of 31 days in the negative day adjustment loop, which doesn't correctly handle the variable length of months or rolling over the month field properly.

Hence, the main fault lies in the logic of line 306 in DurationFormatUtils.formatPeriod where "days += 31;" is hardcoded. This should be replaced with dynamic calculation of the number of days in the previous month depending on the start and end calendar states.

The recent bug reports retrieved do not relate to this issue and can be ignored.

Summary:
- The bug manifests with start dates on December 31 due to fixed 31 days being added when adjusting negative day differences.
- This leads to an incorrect calculation of months difference, returning -2 instead of 9 in the test.
- The fix likely requires computing month lengths dynamically rather than using the fixed 31 days constant in the negative day adjustment loop.

Next, suggested methods to fix will be identified.
org.apache.commons.lang.time.DurationFormatUtils.formatPeriod(long,long,String,boolean,java.util.TimeZone)
org.apache.commons.lang.time.DurationFormatUtils.reduceAndCorrect(java.util.Calendar,java.util.Calendar,int,int)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
